name: Pollen grain
headline: diameter
subtitle: Common ragweed (Ambrosia artemisiifolia) pollen
description: Pollen grains carry the male reproductive cells of seed plants, and their size and surface pattern differ from species to species. A grain of common ragweed pollen is a small spiny sphere with three openings. The PalDat pollen database measures hydrated ragweed grains at 16 to 20 micrometres across.

measures.label: Diameter (hydrated grain)
measures.note: Size of hydrated pollen under light microscopy; shortest and longest diameters both 16-20 µm

facts.text: Ragweed pollen is spheroidal with a spiny (echinate) surface and three short colpori (combined slit-and-pore apertures).
PalDat places ragweed pollen in its 'small' size class, 10 to 25 micrometres.

sources.title: Ambrosia artemisiifolia (diagnosis by S. Sam, H. Halbritter, H. Heigl; published 2020-12-17)

caveats: Pollen size varies greatly between plant species; this entry uses common ragweed as the example.
The diameter is for hydrated grains; dry grains shrink and change outline.
No source giving the mass of a single ragweed pollen grain was found, so mass is left out.
